chunks: And Ishaq ibn Ammar narrated from Abu al-‘Utārid, who said:

I said to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: A man buys food, then its price changes before he takes possession of it. He said: “Indeed, I like that he fulfill it for him, just as if there had been an increase in it, he would have taken it.”

key_terms.الطَّعَامَ: food being purchased in the transaction
key_terms.سِعْرُهُ: its market price or sale price
key_terms.فَضْلٌ: an increase or added gain in value

ai.seo_question: What should be done if the price of purchased food changes before possession is taken?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses a commercial transaction in which the market price of food changes before the buyer takes possession. Imam Abu Abdillah عليه السلام indicates a preference for honoring the original agreement, reflecting fairness and consistency in dealing when one would have accepted gain had the price moved in the opposite direction.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.3775 - Ishaq ibn Ammar narrated from Abu Al-Utard who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (as) about a man who purchases food, and its price changes before he takes possession of it.
Imam (as) said: "I prefer that he honors the agreement (at the original price), just as he would have taken the benefit if there had been an increase in value."
